name: Joe Bugner
milestone_by_age_26: Won the ABA light heavyweight title at age 17 in 1967 and turned professional the same year, later winning the British and Commonwealth heavyweight titles at 21 in 1971.
early_history_summary: Bugner was born in Hungary and fled to the UK with his family after the 1956 Soviet invasion. He excelled at school sports, winning the national junior discus championship in 1964, and took up boxing at the Bedford Boys Club under Paul King and later Andy Smith, who guided him to turn professional at 17.
family_context_summary: Born to a single mother in Szőreg, Hungary; the family fled as refugees to the UK after the 1956 Soviet invasion, settling in modest circumstances in Huntingdonshire.
primary_early_advantage_tags: refugee background, physical talent, early boxing training, ABA pipeline
evidence_summary: Bugner was a Hungarian refugee who settled in the UK and found boxing through the Bedford Boys Club. His physical gifts (6'4", national junior discus champion) translated quickly to boxing, and with trainers Paul King and Andy Smith, he won the ABA light heavyweight title at 17 and turned professional the same year. His refugee background and single-parent upbringing provided adversity but no documented family domain advantage or financial platform.
starting_point: Born to a single mother in Szőreg, Hungary; the family fled as refugees to the UK after the 1956 Soviet invasion, settling in modest circumstances in St Ives, Huntingdonshire.
current_position: Died 1 September 2025 in Brisbane, Australia, at age 75; final status was retired heavyweight boxer with 69 wins in 83 fights, having held British, Commonwealth, and European heavyweight titles.

trajectory.event: Won the ABA light heavyweight title and turned professional, making his pro debut on 20 December 1967.
Beat Henry Cooper to win the British and Commonwealth heavyweight titles.
Won the EBU European Heavyweight Championship.
Fought Muhammad Ali in Kuala Lumpur, losing by unanimous decision.
Lost a split decision to Ron Lyle in Las Vegas, marking the end of his peak years.
Lost to Frank Bruno at White Hart Lane in a high-profile British heavyweight clash.
Retired from boxing for good after winning the Australian heavyweight title and WBF title.
Died on 1 September 2025 in Brisbane, Australia.

name: Ian O'Brien
milestone_by_age_26: Won three gold medals at the 1962 British Empire and Commonwealth Games at age 15, then Olympic gold in the 200m breaststroke at the 1964 Tokyo Olympics at age 17 in world record time.
early_history_summary: O'Brien was a breaststroke swimmer from New South Wales who was a protégé of coach Terry Gathercole (assisting Forbes Carlile). He had his first taste of international competition at 15, winning the national 220 yards breaststroke title in 1962 and earning selection for the Commonwealth Games in Perth.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Australian swimming pipeline, elite coaching, early international competition, Forbes Carlile system
evidence_summary: O'Brien was a breaststroke prodigy from New South Wales who benefited from Australia's elite swimming infrastructure. Under coaches Terry Gathercole and Don Talbot, and within the Forbes Carlile system, he won Commonwealth Games gold at 15 and Olympic gold at 17 in world record time. No family background or financial platform is documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born 3 March 1947 in Wellington, New South Wales, Australia; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from competitive swimming after the 1968 Olympics; later worked in the television industry. Currently living at age 78.

trajectory.event: Won three gold medals at the British Empire and Commonwealth Games in Perth, including both breaststroke events and the medley relay.
Won Olympic gold in the 200m breaststroke at the Tokyo Olympics in world record time (2:27.8), plus a bronze in the medley relay.
Successfully defended both breaststroke titles at the Commonwealth Games in Kingston, Jamaica.
Came out of retirement for the Mexico City Olympics, finishing sixth in the 100m breaststroke, then retired permanently.
Living in retirement in Australia.

parent_family_domain_summary: Mother was an educator who co-owned a private Montessori school; father was a grocer. No direct technology or internet domain transfer documented.

name: Hyun Jung-hwa

early_history_summary: A table tennis prodigy from Busan, South Korea, Hyun rose through the national team system to win her first World Championship gold at 17. She was considered a key player in South Korea's golden age of table tennis, known for her emotional control and come-from-behind victories.

She won her first World Championship gold in women's doubles at 17 and Olympic gold at 19, benefiting from elite doubles partnerships and the Korean national team infrastructure. No family background or financial platform is documented in reviewed sources.
starting_point: Born 6 October 1969 in Busan, South Korea; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Retired from competitive table tennis; coached the South Korean national table tennis team from 2009 to the 2012 London Olympics. Currently living at age 56.

trajectory.event: Won women's doubles gold at the World Table Tennis Championships in New Delhi, partnering Yang Young-Ja.
Won Olympic gold in women's doubles at the Seoul Olympics, partnering Yang Young-Ja.

Won bronze medals in both singles and doubles at the Barcelona Olympics.
Won the women's singles world title at the World Championships in Gothenburg, achieving a career Grand Slam.
Became the first Korean table tennis player inducted into the ITTF Hall of Fame.

name: Fatboy Slim
milestone_by_age_26: As bassist of the Housemartins, achieved a UK number-one single with 'Caravan of Love' in December 1986 at age 23.
early_history_summary: Born in Bromley, Kent; started a punk fanzine as a teenager and met Paul Heaton at sixth-form college. Joined the Housemartins as bassist in 1985 at age 22, replacing the original bass player, and the band achieved a UK number-one single the following year.
family_context_summary: Born to a teacher mother and an environmentalist consultant father (appointed OBE). Middle-class upbringing in Reigate, Surrey. Family belonged to the Kosmon faith.

His early success was driven primarily by the high-trust peer collaboration with Heaton and the Housemartins within the fertile UK indie pop scene.
starting_point: Born Quentin Leo Cook on 31 July 1963 in Bromley, Kent, to a teacher mother and an environmentalist consultant father (appointed OBE); middle-class upbringing in Reigate, Surrey.
current_position: Active DJ and musician touring internationally; resides in Brighton, England. Separated from Zoe Ball in 2016. Net worth estimated in the millions from a decades-long music career.

name: Niklaus Wirth
milestone_by_age_26: Earned his ETH Zurich engineering degree in 1959 (age 25) and M.Sc. from Laval University in 1960 (age 26), but his pioneering programming language work (Euler 1965, Pascal 1970) and Turing Award (1984) all came after age 26. No material career milestone by 26.

family_context_summary: Born to parents who were already over 40; father was a geography and geology teacher at the local Gymnasium, mother took care of the household. Grew up in Winterthur, Switzerland.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was a secondary school geography and geology teacher. No direct computer science or engineering domain transfer documented, though the academic household may have fostered intellectual curiosity.

name: Inese Jaunzeme
milestone_by_age_26: Won the Olympic gold medal in the women's javelin throw at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics at age 24, setting an Olympic record and becoming the first Latvian Olympic champion.
early_history_summary: Born in Pļaviņas, Latvia; was Latvian SSR champion in the javelin in 1952 at age 20. Placed third at the Soviet Championships in 1956 to earn selection for the Olympic team. Was virtually unknown before her Olympic triumph, having never thrown beyond 50 metres prior to the Games.
primary_early_advantage_tags: Soviet sports system, physical talent, Latvian champion, Dynamo Riga
evidence_summary: Jaunzeme was a javelin thrower from Latvia who became the first Latvian Olympic champion at the 1956 Melbourne Olympics at age 24. She was virtually unknown before the Olympics, with only a Latvian SSR title and a bronze at the Soviet Championships to her name. Her achievement appears driven by individual talent and training within the Soviet sports system rather than documented family advantages.
starting_point: Born 21 May 1932 in Pļaviņas, Latvia; family background not documented in reviewed sources.
current_position: Died 13 February 2011 in Riga, Latvia, at age 78; final roles were orthopedics professor at Riga Medical Institute and president of the Latvian Olympians Association (1999-2011).

trajectory.event: Won the Latvian SSR javelin championship.

name: Nicola Pietrangeli
milestone_by_age_26: Won the French Championships mixed doubles title in 1958 at age 24, followed by the French Championships singles title in 1959 at age 25, becoming the first Italian to win a Grand Slam singles title.
early_history_summary: Born in Tunis to an Italian amateur tennis player father and a Russian noble mother. Began playing tennis in a WWII internment camp where his father laid out a court. Family settled in Rome in 1946. Made international debut at the 1952 Italian Open and was also a talented footballer, playing for Lazio's youth team, before choosing tennis.
family_context_summary: Born to Giulio Pietrangeli, an Italian businessman and amateur tennis player, and Anna Chirinskaya, a Russian noble whose Danish colonel father fled the October Revolution. Cosmopolitan, multilingual upbringing across Tunisia and Rome.
parent_family_domain_summary: Father was an amateur tennis player who taught Nicola the rudiments of the game in a WWII internment camp, laying out a court inside the camp and providing direct early coaching.
primary_early_advantage_tags: father tennis player, family-domain teaching, internment camp tennis, Rome tennis clubs, cosmopolitan background
evidence_summary: Pietrangeli was born in Tunis to an Italian amateur tennis player father and a Russian noble mother. His father taught him tennis in a WWII internment camp, providing direct domain apprenticeship. After the family settled in Rome in 1946, he developed at leading Roman tennis clubs and made his international debut at 19. He won his first Grand Slam title (French mixed doubles) at 24 and the French singles at 25, becoming the first Italian Grand Slam singles champion.
starting_point: Born 11 September 1933 in Tunis, French protectorate of Tunisia, to an Italian businessman and amateur tennis player father and a Russian noble mother; cosmopolitan, multilingual family displaced by WWII.
current_position: Died 1 December 2025 in Rome, Italy, at age 92; final status was retired Italian tennis legend, two-time French Championships singles winner, Davis Cup all-time wins leader, and International Tennis Hall of Fame inductee.

Died on 1 December 2025 in Rome, Italy.
